newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen higher on Dow, peso stronger.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen higher on Dow, peso stronger.

text.p: -- Mexico stocks seen up on Dow, but awaiting Cetes
-- Peso likely strong on lower U.S. long bond yield
-- Overnight Cetes rate viewed down on strong peso

Dealers saw stocks opening with upside potential on an expected bullish start on Wall Street, although gains could be contained by the outlook for primary interest rates at the Cetes auction later in the day.
"It looks good, we've lagged far behind the Dow, the market hasn't run out of gas yet," one desk trader said.
Analysts situated resistance for the IPC index at 3,960 points, compared to Monday's close of 3,930.09.

The money and foreign exchange markets were both expected to open strong on a favorable reaction in the U.S. bond market to U.S. retail sales data. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 1/32 to yield 6.88 percent in early trade.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.8950/7.9100 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9030/7.9130 per dollar, compared to Monday's close of 7.9090/7.9120.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening down on forecasts of a strong opening for the peso and lower U.S. long bond yields.
